stories.headline: Broncos suspend running back J.K. Dobbins for conduct detrimental to the team
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos will play their Week 12 game at the Pittsburgh Steelers without running back J.K. Dobbins. Coach Sean Payton suspended him for conduct detrimental to the team.

Payton said Dobbins will not practice this week and will not play Friday in Pittsburgh. Reports describe Dobbins as a running back carrying a contract of roughly $16 million.

The Broncos have moved to maneuver around the suspension. Rookie Jonah Coleman scored three touchdowns in Denver's 38-24 win over the Raiders last week, which has put him in a larger role in the offense.

The suspension comes as Denver prepares for a short-week Friday matchup on the road, and the team will adjust its backfield rotation before kickoff.

stories.headline: Blackwood makes 28 saves as Avalanche blank Canadiens 6-0 in Makar's return
stories.summary:
Mackenzie Blackwood made 28 saves, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Montreal Canadiens 6-0 at Ball Arena on Wednesday. It was the team's third straight shutout win at home. It was only the second time in franchise history, including the Quebec Nordiques years, that Colorado has done that. The other came in November 2001.

Devon Toews scored twice. Martin Necas had a goal and two assists, and Artturi Lehkonen had a goal and an assist. Logan O'Connor opened the scoring at 9:43 of the first period, his first goal since March 31, 2025.

Cale Makar had three assists in his return after missing three games with a lower-body injury. Toews called him the best defenseman in the world. The Avalanche improved to 14-7-3 and have won five of their past seven.

Coach Jared Bednar said the team is starting to string together games played the way it wants. Montreal has lost three straight.

stories.headline: Nuggets coach Adelman weighs lineup changes after 120-101 loss to Mavericks
stories.summary:
Denver Nuggets coach David Adelman said changes to his rotation could be coming after Tuesday's 120-101 loss to the Dallas Mavericks. He said it is not too early to consider them and that conversations among the staff have been extensive.

The backup point guard spot is a key concern. Tyus Jones has held it while Julian Strawther began the season injured. Strawther is no longer listed as injured and has been cleared, which points to an imminent return. The Nuggets' reserves are averaging only 28.4 points per game.

Adelman said the starters, led by Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, were not good. Dallas closed the first half on a 15-0 run. The loss dropped Denver to 10-6 and effectively ended its chances of advancing in the NBA Cup.

The Nuggets visit the Utah Jazz on Friday and then play the Toronto Raptors on Sunday.

stories.headline: Republican lawmaker warns governor-elect against altering voter-approved sports measures
stories.summary:
State Rep. Brandi Bradley, a Republican, says incoming Democratic Gov. Phil Weiser should not try to change Colorado's recently passed ballot initiatives on girls' sports and related protections. She warned of a legislative fight if Democrats try to revise them.

The measures take effect Jan. 1, 2027. A Colorado High School Activities Association spokesperson said that, like every member school, CHSAA must comply with the new law. Demonstrators in Denver have called for repeal.

The next test comes when the legislature convenes in early January, shortly after the measures take effect. Democrats hold the governor's office and the statewide offices. Any bill to revise either measure would turn on a simple majority vote, and Bradley and her Republican colleagues have said they will contest it.

stories.headline: Private developers pitch observation wheel, tower and gondola for downtown Denver
stories.summary:
Private-sector proponents are pitching major new attractions for downtown Denver. They include an observation wheel, a tower and a gondola, which they say could reshape the city's skyline and draw millions of visitors to the urban core.

The Denver Business Journal reports that the city is not yet sold on the proposals. Details on sites, costs and timelines remain limited as the concepts are in the early stages.

The pitches come as downtown Denver continues to seek ways to bring visitors and activity back to the urban core. Any project would likely need city review and approvals before moving forward.

stories.headline: Three Rackets to open padel, pickleball and squash facility in Broomfield on Dec. 7
stories.summary:
Three Rackets will open its 34,000-square-foot Broomfield facility on Dec. 7. The venue will offer padel, pickleball and squash courts in a renovated warehouse.

The opening adds to a growing set of racket-sport venues in the Denver metro area, where demand for pickleball and padel has been rising. Denver Country Club also recently announced plans for padel courts.

The Denver Business Journal reported the opening date and the mix of court types. The facility converts an existing warehouse building into an indoor recreation space.

stories.headline: Denver launches pilot study to limit car traffic through Cheesman Park
stories.summary:
Denver's Department of Transportation and Infrastructure is launching a pilot study to reduce traffic near Cheesman Park. Under the pilot, drivers will be limited in the park, while buses, bikes and pedestrians remain welcome.

DOTI oversees the city's streets, sidewalks and transportation programs. Denver Parks and Recreation manages the park's roads and pavilion. RTD operates bus service across the metro area, including routes that serve the neighborhood.

The pilot is intended to gather data on how reduced vehicle access changes use of the park. Residents who drive through or park near Cheesman Park should expect changed traffic rules during the study period.

stories.headline: Colorado's waste diversion rate improves to 16.7% as composting programs expand
stories.summary:
Colorado diverted 16.7% of its waste from municipal landfills in 2025, up from 15.7% in 2024. The figure comes from the 10th annual State of Recycling report, based on Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment statistics. The report was produced by CoPIRG and Eco-Cycle.

Expanded composting drove much of the gain. Colorado diverted 29% more food scraps and yard trimmings in 2025 than in 2023. Denver has diverted nearly 68,000 tons of organic waste since 2023 by adding 50,000 households to its compost routes. Longmont's commercial diversion rate rose to 62% from 35%.

The report credits a 2022 state law with helping Colorado avoid between 4.1 billion and 5.8 billion single-use plastic bags. At least 23 communities now guarantee recycling access for single-family homes, up from 12 in 2017.

Advocates say a 2022 packaging law, which charges producers fees and sends millions of dollars to communities, should accelerate progress. Grants are going to towns such as Dolores and Cortez, with applications open to others.

stories.headline: Douglas County's Link On Demand ride service expands to Sterling Ranch and Roxborough
stories.summary:
Douglas County's Link On Demand micromobility service will begin serving Sterling Ranch and Roxborough on Friday. Residents there will be able to request rides to and from those areas.

County commissioners approved a $2.375 million contract on Nov. 3 with River North Transit LLC, a subsidiary of Via Transportation. The contract covers the Highlands Ranch service area and the expansion through July 2027. The expansion is expected to cost about $500,000 annually. A $1.5 million RTD grant for Highlands Ranch operations over three years freed up money to make it possible.

The service began in Lone Tree in 2012 as a free shuttle and now also serves Meridian, Highlands Ranch, Stonegate, Parker and Castle Rock. It has completed more than 350,000 trips. Commissioners celebrated the expansion at a Sterling Ranch event.

Link On Demand runs Monday through Saturday and includes accessible vehicles. Riders can book through the app or by calling 719-212-2430.

stories.headline: Denver Rescue Mission hands out more than 3,500 Thanksgiving meals amid record requests for help
stories.summary:
The Denver Rescue Mission and dozens of volunteers distributed more than 3,500 Thanksgiving meals Tuesday at a drive-thru event outside Empower Field at Mile High.

The organization's CEO said more people than ever have asked for help this year. The record demand reflects ongoing pressure on households in the Denver area.

Volunteers packed and handed out meals to people in need ahead of the holiday. The event is one of several Thanksgiving food efforts across the metro area.

stories.headline: Low snowpack in northern Colorado mountains 'eerily similar' to last year, experts say
stories.summary:
Statewide snowpack stood at 75% of normal as of Nov. 25, with a little over 2 inches of snow-water equivalent, according to the Colorado Snow Survey. The slow start follows a winter in which much of the West had its worst snowpack on record.

The Colorado River Headwaters region, which includes the I-70 corridor and ski areas such as Vail, Breckenridge and Winter Park, was at 54% of normal. The Yampa Valley was at 36%, and the Front Range at 30%. The San Juan Mountains were at roughly 160% after historic late-October and early-November precipitation, and the Gunnison area was at about 110%.

Assistant State Climatologist Peter Goble called the northern trends eerily similar to last year but said many months of winter remain. He said it is statistically unlikely to be as bad as last year, but not impossible.

Summit, Eagle and Grand counties and parts of Routt County remain in exceptional drought, the highest level, according to the latest U.S. Drought Monitor.

stories.headline: Wolf Creek tops Colorado with 72 inches of snow as storms approach northern mountains
stories.summary:
Wolf Creek Ski Area near Pagosa Springs leads Colorado resorts in season snowfall at 72 inches, well ahead of its closest competitors. Southwest Colorado is the only part of the state with above-normal snowpack, at about 162% of normal in the San Miguel-Dolores-Animas-San Juan basin.

A change appears to be coming. OpenSnow's five-day forecast shows Steamboat Resort likely to get the most new snow at 11 inches. Arapahoe Basin and Loveland are each forecast to get nine inches. The brunt is expected Saturday and Sunday, with three more storms possible in the first 10 days of December.

Northern and Northwest Colorado remain notably dry, at about 31% and 34% of normal. A longer-range Pivotal Weather forecast shows about seven inches of snow possible in the Denver metro area over the next two weeks. That would be the first significant snowfall along the I-25 corridor this season, though the forecast is more than a week out and could change.

weather.notable: Nearly 9 degrees above the average high for this time of year.

topStory.headline: Storms Disrupt Thanksgiving Travel as Macy's Parade Is Postponed for First Time in Its History
topStory.summary:
A powerful storm system moving up the U.S. East Coast is disrupting Thanksgiving travel, prompting New York officials to postpone the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday. It is the first postponement in the parade's 100-year history. The parade was not held from 1942 to 1944 because of World War II, and in 1971 the balloons were grounded by strong winds but the parade went ahead. Thousands of flights have been canceled or delayed on one of the busiest travel days of the year, and families are reporting standstill traffic on roads. NBC News reported more than 300 flights canceled as of its latest update.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency for New York City, including the Bronx, Kings, Queens, New York and Richmond counties, as well as Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester counties and contiguous counties. Hochul said state resources were ready to respond and to keep the power on, and she urged residents to "stay prepared, stay alert, stay informed and stay vigilant." New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani issued a travel advisory saying the worst of the storm was expected to hit the city from Thursday afternoon into late Thursday night. He urged travelers to budget extra time, leave early, and stay indoors if conditions become severe, saying, "There is no destination worth risking your safety."

More than 80 million people were under weather alerts Wednesday, with the National Weather Service warning of gusts as strong as 70 mph from South Carolina to Massachusetts. A relatively rare High Wind Warning was issued for New York City, where gusts could reach 60 mph, and a wind advisory is in effect from 10 a.m. Thursday to 1 a.m. Friday in parts of northeast New Jersey and southeast New York. Forecasters also warned of heavy rain, coastal flooding, downed trees and power outages. Up to 5 inches of rain could fall in parts of the Southeast, including Florida and the Carolinas, where damaging winds, tornadoes and waterspouts are possible. The system already dropped more than half a foot of rain on Miami, causing flooding in South Florida.

Snow is forecast for parts of the interior East and the Midwest, some of which could see their first measurable snowfall of the season. Winter storm warnings and advisories were issued for parts of Illinois and Missouri, including St. Louis, through Thursday evening, with up to 6 inches expected and as much as 9 inches in some areas. Boston, Philadelphia and Washington, D.C., were expected to see chilly rain but to be spared the heaviest totals. In Miami, a FedEx cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport at about 8:40 p.m. Wednesday, temporarily closing all but one runway; no injuries were reported.

The disruptions come as AAA estimated 81.5 million Americans would travel at least 50 miles from home for the holiday. Weather.com reported that a separate set of storms is affecting the West Coast, where rain and repeated king tide flooding have hit areas such as Pacifica, California, with residents evacuating flooded homes. Travel problems are expected to continue through Thursday and into the weekend, and the rescheduled parade on Saturday will depend on conditions in New York City. Travelers are being advised to check with airlines and local authorities for the latest updates.
